ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Buriat (buri1258).

notes: Research. Buriat (Buryat) is a Mongolic language written in a Cyrillic alphabet (Poppe 1960) that extends Russian with three letters: Ү (close front rounded /y/), Ө (close-mid front rounded /ø/) and Һ (/h/). The map covers the base Cyrillic inventory plus these and encodes phonemic long vowels, which Buriat writes as doubled vowel letters (аа, ээ, оо, өө, уу, үү …), via longest-match digraph entries. The short-vowel qualities are corrected against gold pronunciations: ⟨э⟩/⟨ээ⟩ are open-mid [ɛ(ː)] (not close-mid [e(ː)]), ⟨о⟩ is open-mid back [ɔ] (not [o]), and ⟨ү⟩/⟨үү⟩ are front rounded [y(ː)] (not [ʊ(ː)]) — matching the Khalkha-type Mongolic vowel space Poppe (1960) describes. Word-final ⟨н⟩ realises as the velar nasal [ŋ] (Poppe 1960; e.g. шэхэн [ʃɛxɛŋ]), modelled as a `word_final` positional override; ⟨б⟩ devoices to [p] before a voiceless consonant, modelled as an allophone rule. Word stress is non-contrastive and generally falls on the last syllable of the (mostly disyllabic) stem in the sampled forms; marked here as final by default. Vowel harmony and the reduced quality of unstressed vowels are conditioned rather than spelled and are left unencoded; Russian loanword letters (в ф ц щ) keep their Russian values.
